technical-data.invention-title: BELLOWS ACTUATION DEVICE, SPECIALLY FOR ROBOTIC MANIPULATOR, AND METHOD TO OPERATE SAID DEVICE
DISPOSITIF ACTIONNEUR DE SOUFFLETS, SPECIALEMENT POUR MANIPULATION ROBOTIQUE, ET PROCEDE DE FONCTIONNEMENT DUDIT DISPOSITIF
DISPOSITIVO DI ATTAZIONE A SOFFIETTO, SPECIALMENTE PER MANIPOLATORE ROBOTICO, E METODO DI AZIONAMENTO DI DETTO DISPOSITIVO

nplcit.text: PATENT ABSTRACTS OF JAPAN vol. 018, no. 538 (M-1686), 13 October 1994 (1994-10-13) & JP 06 190771 A (TOYOTA MOTOR CORP), 12 July 1994 (1994-07-12)
PATENT ABSTRACTS OF JAPAN vol. 1997, no. 04, 30 April 1997 (1997-04-30) & JP 08 323675 A (KUBOTA CORP), 10 December 1996 (1996-12-10)

abstract.p: It is described an actuation device using, for the active element, a flexible bellows operated by a pressurized fluid (usually, but not necessarily, at a pressure higher than the ambient one). The bellows is housed, for the most part of its length, inside a cylindrical cavity having the inner diameter slightly larger than the bellows outer one, so that the bellows is free to vary its length, but is restrained to bend sideways and therefore can be operated by high pressure.

La présente invention concerne un dispositif actionneur utilisant, comme élément actif, un soufflet souple mis en oeuvre à l'aide de fluide pressurisé (habituellement, mais pas obligatoirement, à une pression plus élevée que la pression atmosphérique). Le soufflet est logé, pour la plus grande partie de sa longueur, dans un compartiment cylindrique dont le diamètre intérieur est légèrement plus grand que le diamètre extérieur du soufflet, de manière à ce que le soufflet puisse librement varier dans sa longueur, mais soit empêché de se courber latéralement, et puisse ainsi fonctionner à des pressions élevées.

description.p: DESCRIPTION
Bellows actuation device, specially for robotic manipulator, and method to operate said device
TEXT OF THE DESCRIPTION The invention relates to a bellows actuation device, specially for robotic manipulator, and a method to operate said device.

Industrial robotic manipulators known in the art are mainly devised to handle, objects having a hard structure and usually a good resistance, therefore they are usually well suited for industrial applications where a sure hold of hard and solid objects is required (e.g., metal pipes largely used in ofF-shore structures). New requests are rising for robotic devices to be used, for example for scientific research activities (e.g., for biology, archaeology, geology, etc.), for example in the underwater field. This type of use requires the ability to handle and grasp fragile, delicate, and, often, soft objects, that are likely to be damaged if handled with conventional devices.

In order to prevent the possible damaging of fragile objects, it could be possible to provide the manipulator with tactile sensors able to measure the force actually applied to the surface of the object, but this solution proves of high complexity, and conspicuous technical problems must be addressed for its implementation in devices for special uses, as, for example the underwater one.

For example it is known from the art a robotic manipulator of the articulated jaw type, described in US-A-4.607.998. The eledrohydrauiic actuatjon system subject of the patent is a two piston-cylinder assembly, fixed volume, hydraulic system operated by an electric motor by means of a screw device. Friction resulting from the piston seals and from the thrust bearings of the screw is necessary for the system operation, and is so tailored as to have an entity that restrains jaw motion due to applied external forces. This characteristic, while proving advantageous when
the handled objects show a solid and hard structure, proves disadvantageous when the objects to be handled are fragile and soft ones, as for biologic specimens, archaeological items, etc.. The object of the invention is to overcome the above drawbacks and to provide an actuation device using, for the active element, a flexible bellows operated by a pressurized fluid. The device subject of the invention solves also another problem in the case long and compliant bellows are used with pressures of the operating fluid of some relevance, according to the preferred embodiments of the invention. Bellows with these characteristics, usually having a high iength-to-diameter ratio, show, starting from very low operating pressure, a structural instability phenomenon, named "buckling", causing an out-of-control sideways deformation and substantially reducing the useful output force as well as the range of motion, making this kind of bellows actually not suited to be used in manipulation devices.

The device subject of the invention comprises, in the basic embodiment, a bellows housed, for the most part of its length, inside a cavity, usually cylindrical in shape, having the inner diameter slightly larger than the bellows outer one, so that the bellows is free to vary its length, but is restrained to bend sideways and therefore can be operated by a pressure fairly higher than the one that would cause the above mentioned instability phenomena in an unrestrained bellows. A specially suitable field of application of this type of actuator is the one of robotic grippers, where it proves more advantageous than solutions based on the use of other devices, like pneumatic or hydraulic piston-cylinder assemblies. To achieve said objects, the subject of the invention is a bellows actuation device, specially for robotic manipulator, and its variant embodiments, as better described in daims 1 to 15 which are integral part of the present description.

Further subject of the invention is a method to operate said device, and its variants, as better described in daims from 16 to 24, which are integral part of the present description.
The bellows actuation device subject of the invention is virtually friction-free, thus allowing to obtain a relation between the operating pressure and the contart force applied to the handled object, that can be represented by a mathematical function without any discontinuity point. These chararteristics make it possible and easy the implementation of an accurate control of the contact force, thus allowing to make robotic manipulators able to handle fragile or delicate objects without damage.

The main advantage of the bellows actuator versus the piston-cylinder assembly is due to the absence of sliding seals and hence to the absence of friction and wear. This characteristic proves very useful for devices intended for handling fragile or delicate objects, allowing to obtain an indirect measurement of the contart force applied to the object by means of a measurement of the operating pressure.

The manipulators that can be realized using the actuation device subject of the invention, characterized by being friction-free, overcome the above-said drawbacks and, when used in association to a suitable servo-control, can achieve a fine regulation of the contact force applied to the object, and hence a sure hold with no risk of damaging the object, without requiring complex tactile sensors.

Moreover, the manipulators subject of the invention have the characteristic to be very easy to implement and are suitable to be made of materials able to withstand fairly well the typical operating conditions of underwater robotics. The main characteristics that are achieved are the followings.

No-friction: as well known, the friction-force vs. motion-speed relation is not only not-linear, but also not-continuous due to the transition between static and dynamic friction (when speed crosses the zero value). The presence of friction in a device that has to transfer force and motion between the actuating section and the actuated one of a manipulator, predudes the continuity of the relation linking the force applied to the object by the manipulator with the force produced by the
driving device, and therefore does not allow to calculate the contart force applied to the object on the basis of the measurement of the force produced by the driving device.

Force Control: the feasibility to easily implement (without the use of spe al sensors) a force control (instead of a position control), makes it possible for the manipulator to have a degree of "compliance", that is the ability to adapt itself to the shape and to small displacements of the manipulated object with no substantial variation of the contact force.

A further advantage of the use of a bellows, is the feasibility to couple directly its ends to members of the manipulation device, each moving with respect to the others, with no need to use joints or couplings, because the bellows flexibility is usually adequate to allow the required degree of flexure^

Further objects and advantages of the invention will be dearly shown in the following detailed description of an example of embodiment and from the attached drawings, given for a non limiting explanatory purpose, where:
Fιg.1 shows a longitudinal section of a first embodiment example of the bellows actuation device subject of the invention;
Fig.2 shows a longitudinal section of a second example of embodiment of the actuation device having an extension of the static member;

Fig.3 shows a longitudinal section of a third example of embodiment of the actuation device having two fingers; Fig.4 shows a longitudinal section of a fourth example of embodiment of the actuation device having a finger able to move in two directions thank to a joint;
Figures from 4a to 4d show transverse sections of different variant embodiments of the moving member shown in Fig.4;

Rg.5 shows a further variant embodiment of the finger having the moving member formed by two phalanges;
Fig.6 shows a possible example of embodiment of a system to operate the device consisting of a fixed-volume hydraulic system.

Flexible bellows are tubular elements, usually but not necessarily with cylindrical symmetry, having an undulated wall, formed of a series of convolutions; this spedal shape gives flexible bellows high chararteristics of lateral flexibility and longitudinal compliance, and at the same time good chararteristics of pressure holding resistance.

This makes bellows suitable to be used as actuators having chararteristics similar to the ones of hydraulic or pneumatic piston-cylinder assemblies. In fact they are able to convert the pressure of the inside fluid into mechanical force, following the longitudinal axis, and volume variations of the inside fluid into a displacement of the two ends each with respect to the other.

If the ends of the bellows are connected to two members of a device, each being able to move with respect to the other, it is possible, by pressurizing the inside fluid, not only to obtain the motion of these members each with respect to the other, but also to apply a force to these members and therefore also to other objects in contart with them. The flexible bellows, integrated in a suitable mechanical device, is able to implement the two main functions of a manipulation device: the grasping motion and the grip holding by means of the contact force.

T e main differences between the bellows, used as actuators, and piston-cylinder assemblies are: absence of the friction due to the seals, ability to change in shape by means of lateral flexure, spring-like resistance to variation of length

T e resistance to variation of length is related to the longitudinal spring-rate and, as a consequence, the inside fluid must be pressurized to have a variation of the length of the bellows with reference to the length at rest.
In the use as actuators, best performances are attainable with bellows having a high length to diameter ratio, and hence a low longitudinal spring-rate and a wide length variation range, in that these make possible a wide motion range with low operating pressures.
Rgure 1 shows a longitudinal section of a particular embodiment suitable to implement a part of a manipulator able of rotational motion around an axis.

A moveable member 1, comprising a cylindrical cavity 2 housing a bellows 3, is hinged to the static part 4 by means of a pivot pin 5. The two ends of the bellows are mounted one to the bottom of the cavity of the moveable member and the other to the static member, in face of the cavity. Length variations of the bellows generated by the pressure of a fluid fed through the input 6, cause the rotational motion of the moveable member perpendicular to the rotation axis around pivot pin 5, as shown in the phantom section that schematically represents the motion of the moveable member.

The two ends of the bellows are mounted, by way of example, by elements 7 and 8 that seal the ends to the cavity and the static part, with exception of the fluid input 6, formed, by way of example, by a bore in the mounting element 8.
The mounting elements may be of any suitable known type, by way of example screwed to the moving and static members.

When the moveable member is in contart with an external object, by raising the pressure of the fluid inside the bellows, it is possible to apply a force to that object. As shown in Rg.2, where the same numbers refer to the same elements of Rg.l, if this object is placed between the moveable member 1 and an element 9 solidly mounted to the static member 4 to form an extension of this last fadng the moving part, by means of the control of the fluid pressure it is possible to grasp the object, gripping it between the moveable member 1 and the element 9 fixed to the static part, and to apply a desired contart force, as shown in the phantom section of the drawing that schematically represents the movement of the moveable member.
The device can be advantageously used to implement each finger of a multi-fingered manipulator being spedally easy to be made.

A two fingers manipulator, that can be implemented using two devices of the type shown in Rg.l, having the moveable elements la and lb faced each other, and a common static element 4, is shown, by way of example, in Rg.3, where the same elements of Rg.l are referred to with the same numbers, with the addition of the subscript "a" for the first finger and "b" for the second finger.

A manipulator able to handle fragile objects may be formed of a plurality of fingers, typically three to six, mounted around a central axis, to be able to converge in order to carry out the grasping action: to obtain the desired motion of each finger, it is enough to position suitably the pivoting axes about the pivot pins 5.

As shown in fig.4, where the same elements of Rg.l are referred to with the same numbers, the device subject of the invention allows also to easily implement a finger able to move in two directions. In this kind of implementation, moveable member 1' is mounted on the static member 4 by means of a joint G allowing a two degrees-of-freedom motion about its pivot point, and is equipped by a plurality of bellows 3, typically two to four, each operated independently to each other. Therefore the finger is able to move, not only in the radial plane, but also sidewise in order to optimally position the contart point on the handled object. In this case, the moveable member 1' is made so as to allow the housing of the plurality of bellows, by way of example making a cavity for each bellows.

Said bellows, and relevant housing cavities, are placed, with reference to the finger centerline passing through the joint G, in a way that the resulting force of their individual actions (taking also in account the reaction of the joint) can be oriented along any direction in the plane normal to the finger centerline, depending of the different combination of amplitudes of said individual actions.
Rgures 4a to 4d show orthogonal sections of the moveable member 1' of Rg.4, for some implementation examples of joint-mounted fingers.

Typical symmetrical configurations may use either three bellows (with relevant housing cavities 2) equally spaced (at 120°) with reference to the finger centerline passing through the joint G, or four bellows equally spaced (at 90°), as respectively shown, in a section of the finger normal to the centerline, in figures 4a and 4b.

In case it is preferable to give priority to the ability to work in a given angular sector, where the redprocal converging motion of the fingers, required to grasp objects, proves more important, the bellows may be placed not symmetrically; by way of example, in the case of three bellows, two of these may be spaced of 90° each other and of 135° with reference to the third, as shown in fig.4d.

As an alternative, just two bellows can be used, spaced each other of an angle smaller than 180°, as shown in fig.4c. A further configuration of a finger for robotic manipulator that can be implemented using the device subject of the invention is the one with more than one phalanges, formed of a plurality of devices mounted in series; by way of example and without restriction, a two phalanges configuration is shown in fig.5, where the same elements of the first of the phalanges are referred by the same numbers of fig.l, and the second phalanges is formed of a moveable member 1", with cylindrical cavity 2", pivotally mounted to the moveable member 1 of the first phalanges around pivot pin 5", and a bellows 3" joined to the bellows of the first phalanges by means of a mounting and coupling member 11 having a channel 10 through which the fluid can flow from one member to the other, and terminated at the other end by a mounting element 7. In this configuration, the grasping ability of the manipulator is improved because each finger can dose around the object, as shown in the phantom section of the drawing, sketching the movement of the moveable members.
Moreover, by means of a suitable tailoring of the section areas of the two bellows, the distribution of the contact-force along the finger length can be optimized.

As for concerning the methods of operation that can be used, a pneumatic method may be used: the bellows is fed through the input 6 with pressurized air, the pressure of the air being regulated by means of a valve (or similar device); this method is well suited for terrestrial applications.

A pressure-control hydraulic method can be used as well: the bellows is fed through the input 6 with oil, the pressure of the oil being regulated by means of a valve (or similar device). The device subjert of the invention optimally lends to be operated by a fixed-volume hydraulic system, as described in the following with reference to figure 6, allowing to make manipulators of small dimension, showing high dexterity, suitable to be used underwater and requiring just electric power to be operated.

In such hydraulic system, each of the bellows (slave) SI used to actuate the manipulator, in any of the above described variant embodiments, is coupled to a second bellows (master) S2 by means of a fixed-volume dosed-drcuit filled with not-compressible fluid (e.g., hydraulic oil). The two bellows may be coupled by way of example, by a little pipe T allowing the passage of the fluid among them.

This system is able to transduce a mechanical displacement of the master bellows S2 in a displacement of the slave bellows SI (the amplitude ratio of said displacements being the reverse of the ratio of the equivalent section areas of the two bellows), and to transmit a mechanical force applied to one of the bellows to the other one, being the transmission ratio equal to the ratio of the equivalent section areas of the two bellows.

For the displacement of the master bellows S2, as driving device AT, it may be used either rotational electric motors coupled to a rotary-linear conversion device (by example a sσew device ended with a piston ST), or linear electric motors, by example of the type said "Voice-Coil" where the piston ST is moved by the magnetic force generated by the motor.
The latter, showing virtually no friction, are spedally suited for the implementation of robotic manipulators using the no-friction characteristic of the actuation device to achieve a fine control of the contart force applied to the object.

The master bellows S2 and the slave one SI are coupled by means of a fluid line T, generally flexible and pressure-resistant, forming a fixed-volume hydraulic αrcuit, filled with not- compressible fluid.

The driving device AT, by way of example of the voice-coil type, is coupled to the free end of master bellows S2 so that its line of action is substantially in line with the longitudinal axis of said bellows. By applying a force to the free end of the bellows, the electric motor can produce a longitudinal deformation of the bellows. It follows a volume variation of the master bellows that causes a corresponding amount of fluid to flow to or from the slave bellows, indudng a longitudinal deformation of this last and so transmitting the motion to the device. A further advantageous characteristic of the fixed-volume system of operation, comes from the direct proportionality relation existing between the length variations of the two bellows; that characteristic allows to evaluate with good accuracy the length of the slave bellows on the basis of a measurement of the master bellows one. This allows to avoid to install position transducers on the manipulator, and instead allows to install these into the operating section, therefore in a sheltered location and with less stringent dimensional constrains. In the same manner the remote location of the operating section proves advantageous.
Variants of the above embodiments described by way of example and without restriction are possible without going out of the invention scope.

To optimize the longitudinal deformation range of the bellows, the mounting of moveable member 1 on static member 4 may comprise, in addition to pivot pin 5, a flexible element, like a spring, for compression preloading of the bellows.
Pivot pin 5 may be replaced by a flexible element, like a spring steel thin plate for compression preloading of the bellows.

The outside surface of the finger may be given a suitable shape, in case coated by a protective layer able also to make easier the gripping of objects, like, by way of example, urethane foam. Moveable members may be actuated either pushing or pulling, by orienting the rotation axes around the pivot pins 5 in a suitable direction.

claim.claim-text: CLAIMS

1. Actuation device comprising: a static member (4); at least a moveable member (1), mounted to said static member so as to have at least a degree of freedom with reference to the static member; at least a flexible bellows (3), operated by a pressurized fluid, mounted, at the two ends, to said moveable and static members respectively, so as to produce a motion of said moveable part depending on said operation.

2. Device as in daim 1, characterized in that said moveable part (1) comprises at least a cavity housing said flexible bellows (3) for the most part of its length, said cavity having dimensions slightly larger than the ones of the bellows, so that the bellows is free to vary in length under the action of said operating device, but is restrained to bend sideways.

3. Device as in daim 1 or 2, characterized in that said mounting of moveable member (1) to said static member (4) is made by means of hinging about a pivot pin in the static member, so that length variation of the bellows (3) generated by said operating device, cause the rotational motion of the moveable member in a direction normal to the rotation axis about pivot pin (5).

4. Device as in any of daims from 1 to 3, characterized in that said fluid is fed into said bellows through an input (6) formed in the element (8) mounting the bellows to the static member (6). 5. Device as in any of daims from 1 to 4, characterized in that said static member has an extension (9) fadng said moving part (1), the latter being able to move toward said extension so to grasp objects.

6. Device as in any of daims 1 to 4, characterized in that it comprises one or more further moveable members, each actuated by an own bellows converging against the first moveable member, so to grasp objects.

7. Device as in daim 1 or 2, characterized in that said mounting of moveable member (1) to said static member (4) is made by means of a joint (G) allowing a two degrees-of-freedom motion about its pivot point.
8. Device as in daim 7, chararterized in that said moveable member (1') is actuated by a plurality of flexible bellows housed each one in a cavity made into said moveable member.
9. Device as in daim 8, characterized in that said bellows and relevant housing cavities are placed symmetrically to said joint (G), equally angularly spaced around it.

10. Device as in daim 8, characterized in that said bellows and relevant housing cavities are placed not-symmetricaliy opposed with reference to said joint (G), not-equally angularly spaced around it.

11. Device as in any of the preceding daims, characterized in that said moveable member (1) is formed of two or more members mounted in series where the operating fluid can flow from one member to the other through a channel (10).

12. Device as in any of the preceding daims, characterized in that said moveable members can be actuated either pushing or pulling, by orienting in a suitable direction the pivoting axes about the relevant pivot pins 5 or joints (G).

13. Device as in any of the preceding daims, chararterized in that said moveable members are coated with a protective layer able also to make easier the grasping of objects, like, by way of example, urethane foam. 14. Device as in any of the preceding daims, chararterized in that said mounting of the moveable member (1) to the static member (4) comprises, in addition to pivot pin 5, a flexible element, like a spring, for compression preloading of the bellows.

15. Device as in any of daims from 1 to 13, chararterized in that said mounting of the moveable member (1) to the static member (4) is made by a flexible element, like a spring steel thin plate, able of compression preloading the bellows.
16. Method of operation of the actuation device following any of the preceding daims, chararterized in that said bellows are operated by a system for feeding a pressurized fluid into them.

17. Method as in daim 16, characterized in that said system is a fixed-volume one. 18. Method as in daim 17, chararterized in that each of the bellows of the actuation device is coupled to a second remote bellows (S2) by means of a fixed volume dosed drcuit filled with not- compressible fluid, and in that a driving action on the remote bellows is converted in a corresponding driving action on the bellows of the actuation device

19. Method as in daim 18, chararterized in that said driving action on the remote bellows causes a longitudinal deformation of it, corresponding to a volume variation, and causing a corresponding amount of fluid to flow to or from the bellows of the actuation device, with following longitudinal deformation of this last and transmission of motion to the actuation device.

20. Method as in daim 19, characterized in that the driving action on the remote bellows is made by means of a rotational electric motor coupled to a rotary-linear conversion device driving said remote bellows.

21. Method as in daim 19, chararterized in that the driving action of the remote bellows is made by means of a linear electric motor (AT), where the piston (ST) driven by the motor drives in turn said remote bellows.
22. Method as in daim 21, chararterized in that said motor is of the Voice-Coil type driving said piston by means of magnetic force.
23. Method as in daim 16, chararterized in that said fluid is gaseous, its pressure being regulated by means of a valve.
24. Method as in daim 16, chararterized in that said fluid is liquid, its pressure being regulated by means of a valve.
